description: We are Team Ashuquasar, passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. For the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, we built "THE MACHINES THAT STAYED"—an interactive web archive that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon, Mars, and asteroid Eros. Our project combines historical storytelling with actual scientific data from the NASA Planetary Data System.
summary: THE MACHINES THAT STAYED is an interactive web archive exploring the stories and scientific legacies of NASA equipment left beyond Earth. Through three mission exhibits—Apollo 12 ALSEP on the Moon, the Ingenuity Mars Helicopter, and NEAR Shoemaker at asteroid Eros—the project combines historical storytelling, mission-specific evidence and scientific data exploration. Its Apollo 12 exhibit features an interactive visualization based on actual NASA Planetary Data System observations from the Solar Wind Spectrometer, accompanied by an accessible data table and NASA references. The archive helps visitors discover how humanity's exploration continues to leave meaningful scientific and historical footprints beyond Earth.
details:
The idea

What happens to the machines humanity leaves behind after exploring other worlds?

THE MACHINES THAT STAYED is an interactive storytelling archive created in response to NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's challenge, "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

The project explores three missions across three destinations: the Moon, Mars and asteroid Eros. Rather than presenting only mission summaries, it focuses on the equipment, the evidence it left behind and the scientific legacy that continues after its operational mission.

1. Apollo 12 — The Moon

The Apollo 12 exhibit explores the Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), with particular focus on its Solar Wind Spectrometer.

The exhibit includes a scientific visualization built from 48 consecutive records in NASA's Apollo 12 ALSEP/SWS Solar Wind 28-Second Resolution Tables dataset for November 19, 1969.

Visitors can explore the measurements through an interactive graph, an accessible data table and sample statistics. The exhibit also links to the official NASA Planetary Data System dataset record, NASA historical material and Hamish Lindsay's technical ALSEP history.

The visualization is based on actual NASA observations. The displayed statistics describe the selected 48-record sample, not the entire mission dataset.

2. Ingenuity — Mars

The Ingenuity exhibit tells the story of NASA's Mars Helicopter and its historic achievement of completing 72 flights on Mars.

It highlights the engineering achievement, exploration significance and legacy of a small aircraft that demonstrated powered, controlled flight on another planet.

3. NEAR Shoemaker — Asteroid Eros

The NEAR Shoemaker exhibit explores the spacecraft's mission to asteroid 433 Eros and its remarkable final descent on February 12, 2001.

The spacecraft survived its controlled descent and continued transmitting data until February 28, 2001. The mission collected approximately 160,000 images.

This exhibit highlights the unexpected scientific value of the spacecraft's final moments at Eros.

Interactive features

The web application includes:

  • Three interactive mission exhibits.
  • A mission selector with keyboard navigation.
  • A case-aware Evidence Vault that changes according to the selected mission.
  • An Apollo 12 Solar Wind Spectrometer data visualization.
  • An accessible scientific data table.
  • Mission-specific historical and technical references.
  • An interactive three-question quiz.
  • Accessibility improvements, including a skip link, keyboard controls and focus management.
  • Image error handling and a no-script fallback.

Technology and development

The project was developed as a lightweight web application using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Git and GitHub for version control and source-code hosting.

AI-assisted development tools supported implementation and refinement, while the project content, NASA references, scientific data integration and functionality were reviewed and tested.

Intended impact

The project aims to make the history of off-world exploration more engaging and accessible by connecting real scientific evidence with storytelling. It encourages visitors to look beyond the end of a mission and appreciate the machines, observations and discoveries that remain part of humanity's exploration history.
